title: Silicon Valley sees AI as the solution – for everyone else
excerpt: I don't find the "AI will cause mass unemployment" argument compelling, in fact I see the opposite as being true.
content_html:
I don't find the "AI will cause mass unemployment" argument compelling, in fact I see the opposite as being true.

The reason we are talking so much about that now is that at the current level of productivity, we just don't need as many humans to do the work, as companies can use AI as leverage to not hire as many people.

This i feel will be a short lived period where not everyone has adopted AI to the fullest and thus simply having AI gives you leverage to not hire as many people and still stay competitive. The same thing happened with computers writ large, during the early days the folks that used computers had massive leverage over those that did not.

But what happens in 5-10 years once most orgs standardize on that leverage and everyone has it. All of a sudden that advantage AI gave you over others evaporates and you're right back to how things have always been, that is more humans give you more leverage.

I think once AI is broadly adopted and standardized, there will be an insane boom period for workers.


Even before AI, there was a serious hiring problem in the United States. Companies seem hell bent on not hiring full time employees at a livable wage. I don't blame the technology, but I do blame the greed of business owners and investors.

While its easy to look at the big picture and long term and say everything will all work out, there are so many individuals who are being hurt because of layoffs, reduced hiring, etc. My team is stressed out because they feel an axe hanging over their heads because private equity has declared no more hiring US developers. It's either AI or outsourcing. We should try to be empathetic because real people are losing their livelihoods and the long term isn't going to help them one bit.


It's a globalization problem that countries have a hard time creating policy against. Countries don't have the enforcement power that they used to. The best we have come up with is using our own markets as leverage. In a hundred years I imagine wealth and income will look much more uniform across the world. Unfortunately, right now, we are stuck competing with people who can earn much less than people in the US. Now we have to worry about this AI disaster waiting to happen because countries have no real power to stop it. They say it looks like AI won't destroy jobs, but I think really we are just watching the various legs on a table be kicked out. It will still stand until it doesn't.


In the long term the sun will go red giant and all life on earth will die.

In the short term I still need to eat, and tech integration that takes 20 years in the economy might leave me totally fucked!


This makes the assumption that humans are needed to drive these AI assisted workflows. I don't think that's going to be the case at all.

The majority of office jobs are comprised of many simple tasks that current and, to an even greater extent, future, models can handle with ease.

Not all companies are looking for 10x productivity gains. I assume most of them probably just want to do exactly what they are doing now but with lower costs.


You think? Here's the U.S. unemployment rate during the great depression

        1929: 3.2%
        1930: 8.7%
        1931: 15.9%
        1932: 23.6%
        1933: 24.9% (Peak of the Great Depression)
        1934: 21.7%
        1935: 20.1%
        1936: 16.9%
        1937: 14.3%
        1938: 19.0% (Economic recession during the Depression)
        1939: 17.2%
        1940: 14.6%

It's only a fraction of the effect (and of course there was also over financialization), but 20% of the US population was farm labor in the 20s, that fell substantially (and there was the dust bowl) up through the 40s as tractors replaced a significant fraction of all farm labor (perhaps 1% per year). Efficiency does not always drive consumption.

Sure seems to rhyme. Call it Jevon's Tractor Paradox.

Something else certainly happened in the rest of the world about that time too!


Who's going to buy the results of that extra output while most people are laid off? Where is the growth going to actually come from?

Even before LLMs, the cost of living and finding a job that left any disposal income were major societal issues.


The economics of AI investment don't make sense without the promise of vast displacement of labor. There's a ceiling on how much value can be created for a company simply by them using AI to crank out a higher throughput of TPS reports.


I've been saying "The economics of AI investment don't make sense" for 2 years but this audience in particular doesn't (on the whole) agree.


Yes, the value of TPS reports diminishes with throughput.

That's why Jevon's Paradox is the dumbest meme we've had this year. The parent concept of marginal utility describes why AI isn't that useful.


Using AI as leverage for labor is myopic. The businesses that thrive will be the ones that use it to automate and allow its employees to go deeper and innovate. The fish can rot from the head or not.


I don't broadly disagree and see AI opening up opportunities that didn't exist before but with respect to companies hiring large numbers of people I wonder what the people will be doing?

Come to think of it, I sort of wonder what many people with office jobs now are doing.


trying to reify the proposed efficiency gains they have been told are just out of reach


One sickening idea I had is even more bureaucracy. You know how any big infra project now has tens of thousand of pages of impact reports, studies and so on. With AI it can be easily scaled to millions if not more. Lots of words that then will be ingested by other AIs. All happily burning electricity in the process.

So more documentation that no one will ever read... Both generated and summarised multiple times by AI...


The same thing they are already doing? Being a companion for someone who doesn't want to be alone.

The human touch, if you will, is hard to replicate. Even where AI can convincingly act human, that often isn't enough to satisfy what people feel. Just look at the HN guidelines as a perfect example. "HN is for conversation between humans." If it were about the content then any suitable content would be welcome, regardless of the origin, but people are here under the belief that they are making a connection with other people.

Maybe someday AI will replace the business owners and managers too, but so as long as humans control the resources, they will choose to surround themselves with other humans by expending some of those resources towards those other humans.


So the tendency to hire friends and "cool looking" people instead of smart talented people will get even worse?


Maybe, but the friend list is already exhausted and "cool looking" people tend to not like the idea of you hiring them just because they look cool. Hence diversity hiring: It became understood that attractive women would get the "ick" if you told them that you were hiring them only because they were attractive women, so there had to be cover for as to why they were suddenly getting hired where they previously weren't as we transitioned into a companion-based economy. Its hard to say if that can be replicated again now that we're all in on the ruse. Possible, but no guarantee. We may have already reached the peak.


I don't find the argument that advanced AI will leave 20% of society permanently unemployed particularly compelling


There are places where 20% of society (or more) are unemployed. They're not nice places. They're run by gangs or warlords. They're the kind of place where teenagers sit on steps and just wait for the wrong person to walk past them.


Do those places have gangs and warlords because they have 20%+ unemployment, or do they have 20%+ unemployment because they have gangs and warlords?


I cannot imagine the answer is strictly just one of those two. Young men in particular who have no prospects can and nothing to domesticate them (parents, jobs, relationship prospects) can especially be a lot of trouble.

That said, I'm not particularly convinced that gangs and warlords would suppress employment (if anything, the more organized criminals tend to run protection rackets which sort of require people to have some income they can steal) however they are most certainly reducing the quality of life for people.

Unemployment causing gangs at least feels more plausible, however you seem to have plenty of areas with gang activity that have plenty of employment opportunities as well as social programs. Selling drugs almost certainly makes more money, but comes with much, much higher risks. I might guess that this is more about social mobility than it is about survival, but I don't want to try to over-simplify a complex issue.


Fortunately it's extremely unlikely.

There was a change in the world, which went largely unnoticed - sometime in 2013-2017 the global number of infants peaked, never to recover.

Those 20% would just figure that there's no need to have children when you can just focus on yourself and go largely extinct within a generation, replaced with some people from the higher tiers, but not nearly enough to make up for those who weren't born.

This actually has been happening without AI for a while now, but I imagine technology would accelerate the process.


> Those 20% would just figure that there's no need to have children when you can just focus on yourself and go largely extinct within a generation, replaced with some people from the higher tiers, but not nearly enough to make up for those who weren't born.

A person being _unemployed_ is not a hereditary trait. Also, while it's already pretty wild to effectively claim that about 20% of humanity carries some kind _doomed to be made unemployable by AI_ gene, it's another giant leap beyond that to declaring this cohort will uniformly choose not to reproduce and therefore become extinct.


It doesn't need to be hereditary. Just needs to be in the range where on one hand a person doesn't want the next generation to go through the same and on the other, where making the most out of their current situation means not starting a family.

It's what's happening right now, just with poverty being the largest factor. Gig/minimum wage workers start families considerably less often and no wonder - how they are supposed to?


> males who come from narrow Stem (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) backgrounds

I see, so women from narrow Stem backgrounds would totally handle these issues differently, got it.


I think you left this off.

> the main reason is that they are, overwhelmingly, males

Was that intentional? Do you disagree that tech is overwhelmingly male?

Do you happen to be someone who believes in differences in the sexes? Just curious.


The article clearly implies that one of the reasons why they "talk such nonsense" is because they are male, but no explanation is given - bog standard misandry that I take umbrage with.


I'm going to assume you left it off intentionally if you can't even address it.

Read it again. They narrow it two ways in addition to being male:

"0. but the main reason is that they are, overwhelmingly, males 1. who come from narrow Stem (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) backgrounds 2. and are trapped in a particular mindset that the technology writer Evgeny Morozov called “solutionism”.

It's not that they are male, it males who come from Stem with a particular solution oriented mindset. I think in a different context you would be less offended. We are talking about driven, solution oriented people. It's a bias. Biases are fine, we all have them, this article is just talking about it.

I could ask again, would you agree that there are differences in the sexes? A different set of biases even?


> I'm not offended in the slightest

> what a patronizing and absurd reply

I had to double check my replies! The author, nor me implied it wasn't about being male, in fact it is explicitly called out. Check out this question:

"would you agree that there are differences in the sexes? A different set of biases even?"

What mindless twaddle aren't you tolerating?


Over a billion unique people are using chatgpt,Gemini,Claude every month. You should try asking one of them what they're doing


Maybe you - as in, whoever says that - should go first talk to them, because I don't know any disabled people wanting AI (data set of one).


Funny how these guys never factor construction workers and building contractors into their AI social caste structures.


A bug in the scriptlet I used to post it, which truncated the title as “Silicon Valley sees AI as the solution – for everyone els...”, which I didn’t notice had dropped the third line of the title.


Rather ironically you spend time outside Silicon Valley it would appear those most at risk of “mass unemployment” are the folks full-press pushing AI.

It’s “cool” and the tech is here to stay, but we appear light years away from anything like what was promised from materializing.

The current hype cycle is clearly barreling toward the “trough of disillusionment” phase of the Gartner hype cycle.

The same thing they are already doing? Being a companion for someone who doesn't want to be alone.

The human touch, if you will, is hard to replicate. Even where AI can convincingly act human, that often isn't enough to satisfy what people feel. Just look at the HN guidelines as a perfect example. Fortunately it's extremely unlikely.

There was a change in the world, which went largely unnoticed - sometime in 2013-2017 the global number of infants peaked, never to recover.

Those 20% would just figure that there's no need to have children when you can just focus on yourself and go largely extinct within a generation, replaced with some people from the higher tiers, but not nearly enough to make up for those who weren't born.

This actually has been happening without AI for a while now, but I imagine technology would accelerate the process.

content_html_zh: 我不认为“人工智能会导致大规模失业”的论点令人信服，事实上，我认为相反的情况是正确的。我们现在谈论这么多的原因是，在目前的生产力水平下，我们不需要那么多的人来完成工作，因为公司可以使用人工智能作为杠杆来不雇用那么多人。我觉得这将是一个短暂的时期，不是每个人都充分采用人工智能，因此简单地拥有人工智能可以让你不用雇用那么多人，但仍然保持竞争力。 同样的事情也发生在计算机上，在早期，使用计算机的人比那些不使用计算机的人拥有巨大的影响力。但是，一旦大多数组织标准化了这种影响力并且每个人都拥有它，5-10 年后会发生什么。 突然间，人工智能给你带来的相对于其他人的优势消失了，你又回到了原来的样子，那就是更多的人给了你更多的影响力。我认为，一旦人工智能被广泛采用和标准化，工人将会迎来一个疯狂的繁荣时期。甚至在人工智能出现之前，美国就存在严重的招聘问题。 公司似乎坚决不以足以维持生计的工资雇用全职员工。 我不责怪技术，但我确实责怪企业主和投资者的贪婪。虽然人们很容易着眼于大局和长远，并说一切都会好起来，但有很多人因为裁员、减少招聘等而受到伤害。我的团队压力很大，因为他们感到头上悬着一把斧头，因为私募股权公司宣布不再雇用美国开发商。 要么是人工智能，要么是外包。 我们应该试着表现出同理心，因为真正的人们正在失去生计，从长远来看对他们没有任何帮助。这是一个各国很难制定政策来应对的全球化问题。 各国不再拥有过去那样的执法权力。 我们想出的最好办法就是利用我们自己的市场作为杠杆。 我想象一百年后世界各地的财富和收入将会更加统一。 不幸的是，现在我们不得不与那些收入远低于美国人的人竞争。 现在我们不得不担心这场即将发生的人工智能灾难，因为各国没有真正的权力来阻止它。 他们说人工智能看起来不会破坏工作岗位，但我认为实际上我们只是看着桌子上的各种腿被踢掉。 它仍然会站起来，直到它不再站起来。从长远来看，太阳将变成红巨星，地球上的所有生命都会死亡。从短期来看，我仍然需要吃饭，而经济中需要 20 年的技术整合可能会让我彻底完蛋！这就假设需要人类来驱动这些人工智能辅助的工作流程。 我认为情况根本不会如此。大多数办公室工作都由许多简单的任务组成，当前的模型以及在更大程度上未来的模型都可以轻松处理这些任务。并非所有公司都在寻求 10 倍的生产力提升。 我认为他们中的大多数人可能只想做他们现在正在做的事情，但成本更低。您认为？ 这是大萧条期间美国的失业率 1929年：3.2% 1930年：8.7% 1931年：15.9% 1932年：23.6% 1933年：24.9%（大萧条高峰期） 1934年：21.7% 1935年：20.1% 1936年： 16.9% 1937年：14.3% 1938年：19.0%（大萧条时期的经济衰退） 1939年：17.2% 1940年：14.6%这只是影响的一小部分（当然也有过度金融化的影响），但 20 年代，20% 的美国人口是农业劳动力，到了 40 年代，随着拖拉机取代了所有农业劳动力的很大一部分（可能每年 1%），这一比例大幅下降（并且出现了沙尘暴）。 效率并不总是能推动消费。这似乎是押韵的。 称之为杰文拖拉机悖论。当时世界其他地方肯定也发生了其他事情！当大多数人被解雇时，谁会购买额外产出的结果？ 增长实际上来自哪里？即使在法学硕士之前，生活成本和找到一份留下任何可支配收入的工作都是主要的社会问题。如果不承诺大量劳动力被取代，人工智能投资的经济学就没有意义。 仅使用人工智能来生成更高吞吐量的 TPS 报告，就可以为公司创造多少价值是有上限的。两年来我一直在说“人工智能投资的经济学没有意义”，但这些观众（总体上）尤其不同意。是的，TPS 报告的价值会随着吞吐量而降低。这就是为什么杰文悖论是我们今年遇到的最愚蠢的模因。 边际效用的基本概念描述了为什么人工智能没有那么有用。使用人工智能作为劳动力的杠杆是短视的。 蓬勃发展的企业将是那些使用它来实现自动化并允许员工更深入和创新的企业。 鱼可以从头部腐烂，也可以不腐烂。我并不完全不同意，认为人工智能开辟了以前不存在的机会，但对于雇用大量员工的公司，我想知道这些人会做什么？想一想，我有点想知道现在许多办公室工作的人在做什么。他们被告知，试图具体化拟议的效率提升是遥不可及的我的一个令人作呕的想法是更加官僚主义。 您知道现在任何大型基础设施项目都有数万页的影响报告、研究等。 借助人工智能，它可以轻松扩展到数百万甚至更多。 许多单词将被其他人工智能吸收。 在此过程中所有的人都愉快地燃烧电力。所以没有人会阅读更多的文档...... 均由AI多次生成和汇总...他们已经在做同样的事情了吗？ 成为不想孤独的人的伴侣。如果你愿意的话，人情味是很难复制的。 即使人工智能可以令人信服地扮演人类的角色，这通常也不足以满足人们的感受。 看看 HN 指南就是一个完美的例子。 “HN 是人类之间的对话。” 如果是关于内容，那么任何合适的内容都会受到欢迎，无论其来源如何，但人们在这里相信他们正在与其他人建立联系。也许有一天人工智能也会取代企业主和经理，但只要人类控制着资源，他们就会选择通过将其中一些资源用于其他人类来将自己与其他人类包围。那么雇佣朋友和“看起来很酷”的人而不是聪明的人才的趋势会变得更糟吗？也许吧，但是朋友名单已经用完了，而且“看起来很酷”的人往往不喜欢你仅仅因为他们看起来很酷而雇用他们。 因此，多元化招聘：人们明白，如果你告诉有吸引力的女性你只是因为她们是有吸引力的女性而雇佣她们，那么她们就会感到“恶心”，所以必须有一个借口来解释为什么她们在我们转型为基于伴侣的经济时突然被雇用，而以前却没有被雇用。 既然我们都陷入了这个诡计，很难说这种情况是否可以再次复制。 有可能，但不能保证。 我们可能已经到达顶峰了。我不认为先进人工智能会让社会 20% 的人永久失业的论点特别令人信服有些地方社会 20%（或更多）的人失业。 它们不是好地方。 他们由帮派或军阀管理。 在这种地方，青少年坐在台阶上，等待错误的人从他们身边走过。那些地方是因为失业率超过20%而有帮派和军阀，还是因为有帮派和军阀而失业率超过20%？我无法想象答案只是这两者之一。
